- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–4% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in the 2nd–3rd day of sentiment change.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–3% downward correction for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33” or “-0.33” patterns, model often misreads sentiment; use sentiment as a multiplier (e.g., 0.85–0.95 for positive, 1.05–1.15 for negative) to adjust forecast mean.
